items.title: Luis Conte interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 24, 2025
items.q: my musicians, Mr. Spano was one of my teachers.

ctx.x: That’s really fascinating. I wonder if you had the experience, perhaps at the city college, where you were taking a music course and the professor started talking about Latin music, explaining it, and you’re sitting there thinking hey, I already lived this.

No it didn’t happen that way. It happened the way I’m telling you, but then immediately I said okay I’m taking some classes here, I’m going to – I knew a little bit of theory and solfeggio and things like that on the guitar, so I says I’m going to take some music theory, piano, you know beginning piano and percussion ensemble. And I would go and listen to the noon band, the twelve o’clock band I forget – there was a big band and I would go there and listen and then I eventually asked if I could sit in. I mean –…
If you went to sit in with this band you mentioned, and probably they were playing mostly – well I’ll make an assumption here, swing or perhaps some rock at the time.
